title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 3-4
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 3 to 4 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'योगो योगविदां नेता प्रधानपुरुषेश्वरः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 3 to 4 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 3 to 4.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 3 to 4** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **योगो योगविदां नेता प्रधानपुरुषेश्वरः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**योगो योगविदां नेता प्रधानपुरुषेश्वरः । नारसिंहवपुः श्रीमान्केशवः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥** **सर्वः शर्वः शिवः स्थाणुर्भूतादिर्निधिर् अव्ययः । सम्भवो भावनो भर्ता प्रभवः प्रभुर् ईश्वरः ॥**

He is yoga itself and the guide of every yogi. The Lord of Nature and Spirit is that God of gods. He came as Narasimha for his devotee; Keshava, the glorious, the Supreme Person is he. He is everything, the destroyer of evil, the giver of good. The origin of all beings, a treasure that never runs out, is that God of gods. The Lord who carries and leads us all is he.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 3 to 4 mean?
faq.a: He is yoga itself and the guide of every yogi. The Lord of Nature and Spirit is that God of gods. He came as Narasimha for his devotee; Keshava, the glorious, the Supreme Person is he. He is everything, the destroyer of evil, the giver of good. The origin of all beings, a treasure that never runs out, is that God of gods. The Lord who carries and leads us all is he.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
